requested.text: has an associated <dfn for=request export>service-workers mode</dfn>

nodes.consequence: requests carry a service-workers mode; "none" bypasses service workers
the update check fetches the new script with service workers bypassed: a seed cannot supply its own replacement from its caches (D12 P02, B-08)
a registration becomes stale by elapsed time since its last update check (86400 s), so the browser re-fetches the seed script whenever reachable
registration requires a potentially trustworthy script origin: the seed's home origin must be HTTPS or loopback (D-1)
a failed install discards the installing worker and keeps the active one: an interrupted/broken update cannot replace a working seed (D12 P15)
sandboxed (opaque) frames have no active service worker: a confined generation cannot be served by the seed's router and must be bootstrapped inline (D12 P16, B-10)
object id = SHA-1 over "<type> <size>\0" + content; loose objects are zlib-deflated: the browser object store must hash the header, not the bytes (D12 P09 matched 880/880)

requested.text: Given three arguments, stores the <new-oid> in the <ref>,

nodes.consequence: a ref moves only if its current value is the expected old id: the Factory's fast-forward gate and a browser ref store both need compare-and-set

requested.text: The order of the tree entries is normalized by mktree

nodes.consequence: tree-entry order is normalized by git but the rule is not stated in the documentation: browser-computed tree ids are correct only as far as observed equality with git goes (P09) - the ordering rule is an implementation fact (D17) [GAP]
packfiles start with a signature and a version: history import/export (D12 B-17) needs a pack reader/writer
a repository may use SHA-256 object names (with a SHA-1 compat map): object-hash choice is D-6 (owner)
secure context is decided by the environment's TOP-LEVEL CREATION URL: an opaque sandboxed frame under a loopback top-level is still a secure context (D12 P08/P16 observed exactly this)
loopback 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 are potentially trustworthy: every FactTest browser probe (127.0.0.1) runs in a secure context
an opaque ORIGIN is not trustworthy (origin-keyed checks such as SW registration fail) even though the environment is a secure context by its top-level creation URL
the sandboxed origin flag forces an opaque origin: confined generations cannot reach the Factory origin's storage (D12 B-09 broker requirement)
a [SecureContext] construct is not exposed at all outside a secure context: absence of an API in an insecure context is exposure, not a runtime failure - admission probes must run in a secure context
[EnforceRange] throws instead of wrapping; the JS API emulates it for i64 address values (CL-W7)
IDL bigint conversion is ToBigInt: Numbers are rejected rather than coerced
ToBigInt64 wraps modulo 2^64 after ToBigInt (which throws for Numbers): the membrane must hand BigInt, and values are two's-complement i64

nodes.statement: A secure context is decided by the environment's top-level creation URL, while trust checks on an ORIGIN treat an opaque origin as Not Trustworthy: a sandboxed generation frame under a trustworthy top-level is a secure context with an opaque origin (secure-context APIs exposed; origin storage, SW control and same-origin reach denied).

nodes.statement: A policy-controlled feature whose default allowlist is 'self' is Disabled in a frame that is not same origin with its container unless the container policy (allow attribute) enables it; capability admission inside a confined generation therefore requires an explicit allow= grant AND permission.

nodes.statement: A service worker's update check fetches its script with service workers bypassed and a failed install keeps the active worker: an installed seed can neither replace itself from its own caches nor be broken by an interrupted update, and cannot be updated at all while its origin is unreachable.
